instructions: Crack the 3 eggs into a large bowl, add the 2 tbsp sugar and whisk until they're well mixed and a little frothy.
Add the 1 1/4 cups ricotta, the 3/4 cup buttermilk and the 1/4 tsp salt. Whisk until it's smooth apart from a few small bits of ricotta.
In a second bowl, whisk the 1 1/4 cups flour with the 1 tbsp baking powder. Transfer it into the ricotta mixture and stir with a spatula until there's no dry flour left. A few lumps are fine.
Grate the zest of the lemon straight into the batter and fold it through. Let the batter sit for 10 minutes while the pan heats.
Rinse the blueberries and put them in a bowl for the table.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium for 2 minutes. Melt about 1 tsp of the butter in it and swirl it around.
Drop in the batter about 1/4 cup at a time, leaving room between them. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until bubbles open on top and stay open and the underside is golden.
Flip them and cook the other side for 2 minutes, until golden and springy when you press the middle. Move them to a plate and cover it with a clean towel.

Cook the rest of the batter the same way, adding a little more of the butter to the pan between batches. Turn the heat down a notch if they brown before the middles cook. You'll get about 12 pancakes.
Serve with the blueberries and maple syrup.
method_notes: Both rated versions mix ricotta, eggs and milk first, add the flour and leavening, and cook the batter in a lightly greased pan over medium heat. Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) uses buttermilk and lemon zest, rests the batter 10 to 30 minutes for a fluffier pancake and cooks them 2 to 3 minutes a side. RecipeTin Eats (after Bill Granger's hotcakes) uses regular milk with a teaspoon of vinegar and a little baking soda, makes a slightly thicker batter and serves them with sugared strawberries. Little Broken separates the eggs and folds in whipped whites for a lighter, airier hotcake. This one follows the lead's batch, which makes about 12 larger pancakes for four.
